name: Muscaduddlers
description: The Muscaduddlers were a white greaser gang from Chicago's South Side, active in the 1960s. They hung out at Cornell Square Park and 49th and Loomis. Members wore the linings of leather jackets as vests with a patch depicting a wine bottle with legs and arms — a nod to their name, derived from Muscatel wine. They are associated with the Cornell Park greaser succession, preceded by the Rebels (1950s) and followed by the Cornell Dukes (1970s).
symbols: Wine Bottle With Legs And Arms (Muscatel Wine Logo)
